name: Johnstown
title: Artificial Turf in Johnstown, CO | NoCo Turf Co.
description: Johnstown's 2026 Level 3 watering season ended October 15; lawns get no water until April 15, and new grass needs a Town permit. Its rebate excludes turf.
h1: Johnstown's Level 3 drought schedule made new sod the hard option this year
lede: Johnstown straddles Weld and Larimer counties and treats its own reservoir water, and in 2026 it rationed it: a Level 3 drought schedule, two watering days a week until October 15 and a permit to water new grass.

answer.question: What are Johnstown's 2026 watering rules for a new lawn?
answer.answer: Tight. Johnstown ran a Level 3 drought schedule in 2026: two assigned days a week and no watering from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. until the season ended October 15. Until April 15, only trees and shrubs may be hand watered, on weekends, and new grass is watered only under a Town permit. NoCo Turf Co. installs artificial turf in Johnstown, Colorado, and turf needs none of that watering.

blocks.h2: Two watering days a week in 2026, and none for lawns from October 15 to April 15.
paras: Johnstown moved to a Level 3 drought watering schedule for 2026. From April 20 to October 15, even addresses and HOA common spaces watered Mondays and Thursdays, odd addresses Tuesdays and Fridays, and nobody watered from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. Since the outdoor season ended October 15, the schedule allows only hand watering of trees and shrubs on Saturdays and Sundays.

At Levels 2 and 3, Section 13-151 of the town code allows no outdoor watering from October 15 through April 15 except hand watering of trees and shrubs, and lets newly planted grass be watered only under a permit issued by the Town. A new sod lawn means an application, an assigned schedule and a hard stop in mid-October; an artificial turf area needs no establishment watering at all.

blocks.h2: Johnstown's lawn-replacement rebate excludes turf and closed in June.
paras: The Town's residential lawn-replacement rebate pays up to $2,000 per water account per year, for Town water accounts only, and says artificial turf is not eligible. It stopped taking new 2026 applications on June 15.

blocks.h2: Johnstown treats its own reservoir water and buys the rest from three neighbors.
paras: The Town draws surface water from Johnstown and Lonetree reservoirs and the Home Supply Ditch and treats it at its own plant. It also buys treated water from Little Thompson Water District, Greeley and Central Weld County Water District.

blocks.h2: Johnstown publishes a design guide for each big subdivision.
paras: The Town posts planned-unit-development design guidelines for 2534, Thompson River Ranch, Iron Horse, North Ridge, The Ridge, Mountain View West, Johnstown Plaza, Great Plains Village, Encore and Granary. If your home is in one of them, read its landscape section before you pick a turf area.

On the Larimer County side, Thompson River Ranch is the largest plat at 493 acres, and 2534 covers 380 acres across 51 plats, the newest recorded in 2026. The Larimer-side median lot is about 5,986 square feet.
That was the largest hail NOAA logged near Johnstown from 2011 through 2025. The Greeley UNC station, east of town, averages 58.3 days a year at or above 90°F.

Soil surveys around central Johnstown map mostly low shrink-swell Olney fine sandy loam and Kim loam, with pockets of Nunn clay loam, a series NRCS rates as limited for building because of shrink-swell.

faq.q: Do I need a permit to water new sod in Johnstown?
faq.a: Yes, at Levels 2 and 3, and Johnstown was at Level 3 in 2026. The town code then lets newly planted grass be watered only under a Town permit and allows no lawn watering from October 15 through April 15.

faq.q: Will Johnstown's rebate pay for artificial turf?
faq.a: No. The program says artificial turf is not eligible, and new 2026 applications closed on June 15.

faq.q: Does the Level 3 schedule apply to my HOA's common areas?
faq.a: Yes. In 2026, HOA common spaces and metro districts shared the even addresses' Monday and Thursday slot until October 15, and no one watered between 10 a.m. and 6 p.m.
